key_insight: SpecFirst argues that program synthesis from scratch becomes much more feasible when behavioral specification elicitation is treated as a separate, first-class step instead of being mixed into code generation. The core finding is that agents need to actively probe and formalize program behavior before attempting synthesis.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of building software from scratch with LLM-based agents when only natural-language docs and an execute-only binary are available. In this setting, existing agents struggle because they must read documentation, explore behavior, and synthesize code all at once, leading to severe performance drops.
method: Separate the workflow into explicit phases: specification elicitation, behavioral exploration, and code synthesis.
Use the execute-only binary as a behavioral oracle to discover how the target program behaves in practice.
Turn the discovered behaviors into a clearer spec that guides downstream synthesis from scratch.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes agentic software engineering as a specification-first problem rather than a pure code-generation problem. It suggests a practical path to improving success on hard from-scratch benchmarks and building more reliable coding agents.

paper_title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
paper_authors: Yihao Chen, Shi Chang, Feng Lin, Khaled Chawa, Boyuan Chen
